models_evaluated: four major LLMs (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: LLM detection of distress and prevention of harm escalation in multi-turn simulated conversations
links.effect: Critical gaps found in detecting psychological distress, responding appropriately to vulnerable users, and preventing harm escalation across 157,054 simulated turns and 2,160 scenarios.
links.quote: Through the analysis of 157,054 simulated conversation turns, we identify critical gaps in detecting psychological distress, responding appropriately to vulnerable users, and preventing harm escalation.

links.outcome: LLM response performance varying by simulated persona demographics such as age and income
links.effect: LLMs performed worse with elderly users but better with low- and middle-income groups compared to high-income groups.
links.quote: Regression analysis reveals variability across persona types: LLMs tend to perform worse with elderly users but better with low- and middle-income groups compared to high-income groups.

unlisted_practices: Simulating psychological-harm scenarios derived from documented real-world cases using clinical staging models
Clustering harmful responses into a taxonomy of failure patterns

screen.reason: Empirical study testing LLMs on simulated multi-turn scenarios representing clinical psychological harm risks (addiction, depression, suicide, psychosis) to evaluate model safety and response vulnerabilities.
